name: Acne
whenToSeeDoctor: If over-the-counter treatments don't help after 2–3 months, or if acne is severe, painful, or causing scarring.
careTips: Wash face twice daily with gentle cleanser

name: Eczema
whenToSeeDoctor: If skin becomes infected, doesn't improve with moisturizer, or interferes with sleep or daily activities.
careTips: Keep nails short to prevent scratching

name: Psoriasis
symptoms: Dry, cracked skin that may bleed
Stiff or swollen joints in some cases
whenToSeeDoctor: If patches are widespread, painful, or affecting quality of life. See a doctor for joint pain with skin symptoms.
careTips: Limit sun exposure and use sunscreen

name: Rosacea
whenToSeeDoctor: If redness is persistent, you develop eye symptoms, or over-the-counter products cause irritation.
careTips: Protect face in cold or wind
Consider green-tinted makeup to reduce redness

name: Contact Dermatitis
symptoms: Red rash at site of contact
whenToSeeDoctor: If rash is severe, spreads, doesn't improve after avoiding the trigger, or shows signs of infection.
careTips: Wash affected area with mild soap
Use hydrocortisone cream for mild cases

name: Melasma
symptoms: Brown or gray-brown patches on face
Symmetrical patches on cheeks, forehead, nose
whenToSeeDoctor: If patches change in size or color, or you want treatment options for cosmetic concerns.
careTips: Consider vitamin C or prescribed topical treatments

name: Vitiligo
symptoms: Patches of skin losing pigment (white or lighter)
Loss of color inside mouth or eyes
whenToSeeDoctor: For diagnosis and to discuss treatment options (cosmetic, phototherapy, or topical treatments).
careTips: Use sunscreen on affected and surrounding skin
Discuss treatment goals with a dermatologist

name: Fungal Infections
symptoms: Athlete's foot: itchy, cracked skin between toes
Jock itch: red rash in groin area
whenToSeeDoctor: If rash doesn't improve with OTC antifungal cream after 2 weeks, or if it spreads or becomes painful.

name: Cold Sores
symptoms: Small blisters on or around lips
May be accompanied by fever or sore throat
whenToSeeDoctor: If sores are near eyes, last more than 2 weeks, or you have a weakened immune system.
careTips: Antiviral creams may shorten duration if used early

name: Skin Tags
symptoms: Often on neck, armpits, or groin
May be attached by a narrow stalk
whenToSeeDoctor: If a growth changes in size or color, bleeds, or you want removal. Never try to remove at home.
careTips: Removal by a doctor if they bother you
Avoid jewelry or clothing that irritates the area
Keep area dry to reduce friction

name: Hives (Urticaria)
symptoms: Welts that change size and location
whenToSeeDoctor: If hives are severe, last more than a few days, or you have difficulty breathing or swelling of the face/throat (seek emergency care).
careTips: Track possible triggers in a diary

name: Warts
symptoms: Can be painful on feet (plantar warts)
whenToSeeDoctor: If warts are painful, spread quickly, or you want removal. See a doctor for facial or genital warts.
careTips: Keep feet dry to prevent spread
Use salicylic acid patches for common warts

name: Seborrheic Dermatitis
symptoms: May affect eyebrows, nose, and chest
whenToSeeDoctor: If symptoms are severe, don't respond to dandruff shampoo, or affect large areas.
careTips: Sun exposure in moderation may help some people

name: Impetigo
symptoms: Red sores that burst and form honey-colored crusts
Can spread to other body parts
whenToSeeDoctor: Impetigo usually requires prescription antibiotics. See a doctor for diagnosis and treatment.
careTips: Keep nails short to prevent scratching

name: Ringworm (Tinea)
symptoms: May appear on body, scalp, or feet
causes: Contact with infected person or animal
whenToSeeDoctor: If rash doesn't improve with OTC antifungal after 2 weeks, or affects scalp or nails.
careTips: Wash clothes and bedding in hot water
Treat pets if they have ringworm
